newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $1 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $1 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs early Tuesday sold steady to $1.00 per cwt higher, with gains powered by strong packer demand and light hog supplies, livestock dealers and packer buyers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold at $0.50 higher at $58.00 to $58.50 in the country and $59.00 to $60.00 at plants, sources there said.

Illinois hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 higher at $58.00 to $58.50 in the country and $59.00 to $59.50 at plants. Sales were possible at $60.00 or higher paid by plants for high-quality hogs, sources there said.

Indiana hogs sold $1.00 higher at $57.00 to $58.00 in the country and $59.00 to $60.00 at plants, Indiana sources said. Ohio hogs sold steady to $0.50 higher, with $55.50 to $56.50 paid in the country and $57.50 to $58.50 at plants.
Packer demand reportedly was partially stoked by strong demand for fresh pork loins, sources said.
Fresh bone-in loin prices on supplies weighing 13-18 lbs, on Monday averaged $163.20 per cwt, up from $160.00 on Friday, and $147.00 a week earlier, USDA statistics showed.
Also, overall pork cut-out values rose $0.30 to $0.32 per cwt, USDA reported.
